questions.sectionHeading: Section I (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: To what extent does historical evidence shape the construction of history? Use Sources A and B and at least ONE other source to support your argument.
questions.stimulus:
Source A: an extract from Norman J Wilson, History in Crisis? Recent Directions in Historiography, 2005. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2019 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2019-hsc-history-extension.pdf

Source B: an extract from Giselle Byrnes, The Myths We Live By: Reframing History for the 21st Century, 2012. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2019 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2019-hsc-history-extension.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant issues of historiography
use relevant sources to support your argument
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Demonstrates a critical assessment of the role of evidence in the construction of history ; Supports arguments with integrated and explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates extensive knowledge, clear understanding and critical insight into relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Provides a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

Demonstrates an effective assessment of the role of evidence in the construction of history ; Supports arguments with explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Provides a logical and cohesive response

Demonstrates sound assessment of the role of evidence in the construction of history ; Makes references to Sources A and B and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Provides a coherent response

Demonstrates limited assessment of the role of evidence in the construction of history ; Makes limited references to Sources A and B, and/or ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues ; Provides a limited response

Demonstrates minimal knowledge of the role of evidence in the construction of history ; Makes minimal references to Sources A and/or B and possibly ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates minimal knowledge of historiographical issues ; Provides isolated observations

questions.sectionHeading: Section II (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: How have changing methods of historians shaped interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in your case study?
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of an appropriate case study
engage with the historiography of the areas of debate selected for discussion
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Demonstrates extensive knowledge, clear understanding and critical insight into changing methods of historians that have shaped interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Demonstrates effective integration of the impact of changing methods of historians on interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Communicates a perceptive judgement in a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of changing methods of historians that have shaped interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Demonstrates integration of the impact of changing methods of historians on interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Communicates a reasoned judgement in a logical and cohesive response

Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of changing methods of historians that have shaped interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Demonstrates some integration of the impact of changing methods of historians on interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Communicates a coherent narrative with some attempt at judgement

Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Provides limited reference to methods of historians and/or interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Communicates a limited narrative

Demonstrates minimal knowledge of ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Provides minimal reference to methods of historians and/or interpretations of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Communicates isolated observations
